Debate Ignites Over Passport's Role as Citizenship Proof in India

A controversy has emerged in India regarding whether a passport definitively proves citizenship. This debate was amplified by reports that passport fees are increasing from July 1. The discussion centers on the government's stance, with some outlets reporting that the government itself has expressed doubts about a passport being sole proof of citizenship. This has led to concerns about systemic gaps in proving citizenship and potential wrongful exclusions, particularly during voter-list revisions. The core question raised is what document, if not a passport, serves as definitive proof of Indian citizenship.
